html:
On 1 December 1640 Portuguese nobles rose in Lisbon, ended sixty years of rule by the Spanish kings and proclaimed the Duke of Braganza King John IV. A war with Spain followed until 1668.

Since 1580 the kings of Spain had also been kings of Portugal, in the Iberian Union. Portugal's enemies became Spain's: the Dutch seized Portuguese posts in Asia and in Brazil. When Spain demanded Portuguese troops and taxes, and Catalonia was already in revolt, the Portuguese struck.

With help from France and later England, Portugal won the main battles, and Spain recognised its independence in the Treaty of Lisbon of 1668. The House of Braganza ruled until 1910. To seal the English alliance, Catherine of Braganza married Charles II, bringing Bombay as her dowry. 1 December is a national holiday.
